newsitem.title: USA: Flagstar's Petty resigns as Denny's CEO.
newsitem.headline: Flagstar's Petty resigns as Denny's CEO.

text.p: Restaurant owner Flagstar Co. Inc. said C. Ronald Petty resigned as chief executive and president of its Denny's restaurant subsidiary on Monday.
Flagstar Chairman James Adamson, who will head Denny's until a replacement is found, said Petty left to pursue entrepreneurial interests.

During Petty's 3-1/2 year tenure Denny's has instituted fast track training programmes for minority workers and diversity workshops for all its 50,000 employees, following charges of discrimination against African-American customers between 1987 and 1994.
In December, Denny's agreed to pay a total of $46 million to nearly 300,000 claimants to settle two class-action discrimination lawsuits brought by that began in 1988.

"He (Petty) joined Denny's at perhaps the lowest point in its history and through his vision and determination completely reversed its direction and competitive position in the mid-scale dining segment," Adamson said, adding that a search for a replacement was underway.
Flagstar owns and operates Denny's, Coco's, Carrows, Quincy's Family Steakhouse and El Pollo Loco restaurants, and is the largest franchisee of Hardee's restaurants.
Flagstar's stock was down 19 cents at $2 on Nasdaq at mid-afternoon.
